title: How many books are in a library with thirty shelves?
description: Joseph helps in his school library. The video finds the books on all the shelves by multiplying tens by tens.
teaching_notes: One idea: books on one shelf times the number of shelves, using tens times tens. Watch for children who add forty and thirty.

source: Your turn: a classroom shelf has about 40 books and there ar
video_script.why: The child can now estimate a count by a part and the number of parts, and tries it alone with tens times tens.
video_script.substitution: Treat forty and thirty as tens, multiply four by three, and read the answer in hundreds.
video_script.anchor: Joseph helping in the school library in Mumbai
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu adds forty and thirty. Each of the thirty shelves has forty books of its own, so the books are thirty groups of forty.
video_script.payoff_line: the library has about one thousand two hundred books

final_answer.spoken: about one thousand two hundred books, a four digit number

maths_rules: one shelf: about 40 books; the library: about 30 such shelves
40 = 4 tens and 30 = 3 tens; 4 × 3 = 12; tens × tens = hundreds, so 12 hundreds
1,200 has 4 digits; a 4 digit number is from 1,000 to 9,999
slip: 40 + 30 = 70 joins the two numbers; the books are 30 groups of 40
your turn: 70 packets, about 60 biscuits each: 70 × 60 = 4,200 biscuits; 4 digits; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: books on one shelf times the number of shelves. Wrong idea: add the two numbers. The library shelf stays in the anchor band; the shelf blocks build on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='m49'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m50'/>Joseph helps in the school library in Mumbai.
<bookmark mark='m51'/>One shelf holds about forty books.
<bookmark mark='m52'/>The library has about thirty such shelves.
<bookmark mark='m53'/>About how many books are in the library, and how many digits does that number have?

<bookmark mark='m60'/>Each of the thirty shelves has forty books of its own.
<bookmark mark='m61'/>The library has thirty groups of forty books.

narration: <bookmark mark='m62'/>First multiply four by three, which gives twelve.
<bookmark mark='m63'/>Ten times ten is one hundred, so we have twelve hundreds.
<bookmark mark='m64'/>Twelve hundreds together make one thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='m65'/>The library has about one thousand two hundred books.

beats.on_screen: the number 1,200 splits into four digit boxes: 1, 2, 0, 0; the words four digit number light up
narration: <bookmark mark='m66'/>Count the digits of the number one thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='m67'/>There is a one, a two and two zeros, which makes four digits.
<bookmark mark='m68'/>A four digit number is from one thousand to nine thousand nine hundred and ninety nine.
